answer: Every identity should carry a scarce, slashable stake, not a free keypair. At dawn of each epoch an agent posts a bond and commits to a rotating hardware attestation; a VRF draws a jury that audits a random slice of its work. Jurors who vouch for a clone forfeit their own bond, and a rising tide of failed audits drains a reputation score that gates payouts. Newcomers start in a juniper-thin trust tier with capped earnings, so farming thousands of identities means funding thousands of bonds and risking the whole stack at once, a cost curve no single check could impose.
